## Introduction

#### Data Description
This report analyses a simulated dataset based on Enterics for Global Health (EFGH), a diarrhea surveillance study conducted from 2022–2024 among children in seven LMICs. The data contain information on demographic, clinical, and socioeconomic characteristics for children enrolled in the study. My report will describe enrollment characteristics for N=8,607 children and evaluate the average benefit of antibiotic treatment with respect to day 3 diarrhea duration.

```{r load-data}
data <- readRDS(
  file = here::here("raw_data/sim_data.rds")
)
```

## Results

#### Enrollment Characteristics

```{r table1}
table_one <- readRDS(
  file = here::here("output/table_one.rds")
)
table_one
```

This table shows baseline characteristics of N=8,607 children enrolled in EFGH, among which n=2,626 (31%) received antibiotics. Children enrolled in Bangladesh and Mali had higher prevalence of antibiotics received (36% and 32%, respectively). Children who received antibiotics had higher prevalence of bacterially-attributable diarrhea, lower weight-for-age z-score, and greater wealth compared to children who did not receive antibiotics.


#### Outcomes

```{r figure}
#| fig.align = "center",
#| out.width = "700px"

knitr::include_graphics(
  here::here("output/predicted_diarrhea_probability.png")
)

```

This figure shows the probability a child will have diarrhea on day three following enrollment by whether or not they received antibiotic treatment, adjusted for pathogen diagnostics, clinical, and child-level characteristics. The probability of day three diarrhea is lower among children who received antibiotics compared to those who did not (68.1% vs. 70.5%).
